children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 and still living at home with me. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 18 and living at home with you.

Since Alex is over 16, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he at sixth form, college, doing A-levels, or on an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is studying for his A-levels at the moment. He's still in sixth form.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Since Alex is studying for his A-levels at sixth form, that counts as approved education.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to fully assess your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Now I need to understand a bit more about Alex's situation:

**Does Alex have any paid work? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't have any paid work at the moment. He's just focusing on his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, his other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Does Alex receive any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 18 years old and studying for his A-levels at sixth form, which counts as approved education
- Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who remain in approved education or training
- You live in the UK and Alex lives at home with you, so you're responsible for him
- Alex doesn't work 24 hours or more per week (he has no paid work)
- Alex doesn't receive benefits in his own right
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important things to note:**
- You should inform the Child Benefit Office if Alex's circumstances change (e.g., if he leaves education, starts working 24+ hours per week, or starts claiming benefits)
- If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge
- Child Benefit will stop when Alex turns 20, or if he leaves approved education or training before then

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you're already claiming and just wanted to check continued eligibility, you should be fine to keep receiving it as long as Alex remains in education!
